info.name: E-Bank Microservices via Gateway
info.description: Run with ebank-local.postman_environment.json and the stack up. Every request uses {{baseUrl}} (localhost:8080). Run folders in order. Customer CRUD cleans up its own temporary customer. Each full iteration creates one account on an existing customer; it persists until the banking H2 database restarts. Runtime IDs are captured automatically in collection variables. Resilience probes default to healthy expectations; read their folder instructions for outage/recovery modes.

item.name: resilience
item.description:
Default resilienceMode=healthy: every request expects real customer fields, so a full run is green with the stack up.

For an outage drill, first run the collection normally to capture existingAccountId. Keep ebank-service and the gateway running. Stop customer-service, set resilienceMode=outage, and run only "Open circuit (five probes)". Each response must be HTTP 200 with matching customer ID and "Not available" for firstName, lastName, and email. Five failed lookups open CustomerRestClientfindCustomerByIdLong.

Wait at least 10 seconds without account requests for HALF_OPEN. Restart customer-service and wait for its API and Eureka registration. Set resilienceMode=recovery and run only "Recovery (two probes)". Two successful real-customer lookups close the circuit. If Eureka has not refreshed, wait another open interval and repeat the recovery probes.

Observe states/events directly at http://localhost:8082/actuator/circuitbreakers and /actuator/circuitbreakerevents; these are instructions, not collection requests, because all collection traffic goes through the gateway. The gateway intentionally does not route backend Actuator or MCP endpoints. See ../resilience-test.md for the full drill. Reset resilienceMode=healthy before running the complete collection again. An HTTP runner cannot stop/restart your local Java services automatically.
